system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41:49, PowerShell ran on WS-MLOPEZ-01 as omar.haddad with the command to run the inventory-approved Deploy-Patches.ps1 script from FILE-HD-01. This matches the stated IT patching practice and scheduled business-hours patching.

The PowerShell process launched wusa to install a Windows update package; Windows Update traffic followed, and PowerShell exited at 13:42:39. These events support a patching explanation for the reported brief window, but do not establish the script's contents.

At 13:30, DC-HD-01 issued a Kerberos ticket for ben.carter from WS-MLOPEZ-01, and WS-BCARTER-01 recorded a network logon for ben.carter from that same source IP. At 13:33, DC-HD-01 recorded a network logon for maria.lopez from WS-BCARTER-01's IP. This is cross-workstation account activity that merits clarification; the records do not establish why it occurred.

The proxy recorded a connection to clients4.google.com with a GoogleDriveFS user agent and a later connection to desktop.dropbox.com with a DropboxUpdate user agent. The inventory says these services are not approved; these records show connections, not that files were uploaded or shared.
WS-MLOPEZ-01 made an SMB connection to FILE-HD-01, where a network logon was recorded as ANONYMOUS LOGON. The records do not show the share or resource accessed or whether data was read or changed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records show the PowerShell command line and process lifetime but not the Deploy-Patches.ps1 contents, signature, hash, or script-block execution details.
The proxy records identify service hostnames and user agents, but the supplied evidence does not establish what files, if any, were transferred through Google Drive or Dropbox.
The SMB records do not identify the share or files accessed, and the provided evidence does not show the outcome beyond the recorded network logon.
The supplied activity window may not include the context needed to explain the cross-workstation network logons.
claims_not_established: That the PowerShell activity was malicious; its recorded command and timing are consistent with the stated IT patching procedure.
That the patch script was unmodified or that its execution was authorized in this specific instance.
That the cross-workstation logons represent unauthorized access, credential compromise, or lateral movement.
That Google Drive or Dropbox was used to upload, store, or share organizational data.
That the anonymous SMB logon resulted in access to files or other resources.
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain the exact Deploy-Patches.ps1 version run at 13:41, its hash and signature, and corresponding FILE-HD-01 share-access and patch-deployment records; confirm with omar.haddad that he initiated this deployment.
Review relevant authentication and endpoint records on WS-BCARTER-01 and WS-MLOPEZ-01 around 13:30–13:33 to determine the context and initiating processes for the cross-workstation logons.
Check software inventory and endpoint process telemetry for Google Drive and Dropbox clients, and review available proxy or endpoint transfer records for any file activity.
Review FILE-HD-01 SMB auditing for the 13:43 connection, including share and object access events.
